extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (KIPO context)
extracted.subtask_description: Official Korean Intellectual Property Office guidelines for examining conflicting applications, determining unpatentable inventions (Article 32), and rules/limits/procedures for amending specifications, claims, and drawings under Article 47 of the Korean Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when conflicting application cannot hold prior-filed status
rubrics_metrics.description: When a conflicting application cannot hold the status of a prior-filed application, an examiner shall conduct examination considering that the conflicting application has never been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This directs examiners to ignore such conflicting applications during substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when applicants of conflicting applications differ
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant of the present application and the applicant of the conflicting application are not the same, an examiner shall notify the applicant of the conflicting application of such fact through the On-nara System (Government Electronic Document Management System).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When notifying a ground for rejection to the applicant of the present application, the ground for rejection shall indicate the fact of conflicting relation. Examiner should check whether a request for examination on the conflicting applications is made when consultation is possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation request when conflicting application is laid open and requested for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a conflicting application is laid open and requested for examination, an examiner shall make a request for consultation under the name of the Commissioner of KIPO within a designated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall notify the applicant of a ground for rejection under Article 36(2) or (3) of the Patent Act (other grounds may be included) along with the request for consultation. In principle, request for consultation and ground for rejection should be notified in separate notices, but they may be combined for efficiency where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome after consultation addressing Article 36(2)/(3) grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving a request for consultation, if an applicant addresses a ground for rejection under Article 36(2) or (3) by reporting on the result of consultation and taking measures within a designated period, an examiner shall make a decision to grant a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a ground for rejection exists and has already been notified and not addressed appropriately, the examiner shall make a decision to reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postponement when conflicting application not yet laid open or requested
rubrics_metrics.description: When a conflicting application is yet to be laid open or requested for examination, an examiner shall notify the applicant of the present application of the intention that examination is postponed until the conflicting application is requested for examination or withdrawn or abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification of postponement informs applicants that examination is on hold pending action on the conflicting application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when applicants are identical (conflicting app granted or finally rejected)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a conflicting application is granted with a patent or where a final decision to reject is made to the application on the basis of a ground for rejection specified in Article 36(2) or (3), the examiner shall issue a notice of rejection to the patent applicant under Article 36(2) or (3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another ground for rejection exists it should be included. If a patent is yet to be granted to the conflicting application, examiner may notify other grounds without reviewing Article 36(2)/(3) grounds; failure to remedy notified grounds after amendment can lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rule for final vs first ground for rejection based on amendment dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims of the present application are amended later than the date when claims of the conflicting application are finally amended, the final ground for rejection is notified; otherwise the first ground for rejection is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When consequences of conflicting application are undecided, examiner may notify a ground under Article 36(2)/(3) together with other grounds and should request consultation with the patent applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of designated period after request for consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for consultation and a ground for rejection are notified at the same time, an applicant intending to extend the designated period may make a request for extension of the designated period relating to the submission of a written argument as well as a designated period upon a request for consultation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants can seek extensions for both written-argument submission and consultation response periods when both notices are issued concurrently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment of a patent/utility model does not enable consultation or resolve conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a conflicting application is registered and therefore no consultation can be made, abandoning the patent or the utility model registration would not mean that consultation is possible or the conflicting relation is resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandoning a patent does not have retroactive effect and does not render a registered conflicting application as though never filed; abandoning registration is not equivalent to abandoning an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of invalidation of registered patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application registered for a patent is determined to be invalidated, it shall be deemed never to have been filed, taking into account Article 36(4) and Article 133(3) of the Patent Act of Korea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation of a registration can remove the filing effect retroactively for assessment of conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed abandonment for non-payment of fees after grant
rubrics_metrics.description: After a patent is granted, where patent fee was not paid in due time for grant or for maintenance or for renewal, the patent application is deemed abandoned and thus shall be deemed never to have been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay grant/maintenance/renewal fees can cause the patent to be treated as never filed for conflict purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion to reject on other grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though there exists a conflicting application, an examiner may make a decision to reject based on other grounds for rejection instead of referring to the conflicting application or notifying a ground for rejection based on the conflicting application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Korean Patent Act does not stipulate that an examiner shall make a decision to reject citing every possible ground; examiner may choose efficient grounds (e.g., obvious lack of novelty/inventive step) to refuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of rejecting multiple same-date utility model filings without consultation when lack of novelty/inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than two applications of utility model registration on the same utility innovation are filed on the same date, but the utility model lacks novelty or inventive step, making the decision to reject without conducting ‘consultation proceedings, etc. among applicants’ under Article 7(2) and (6) of the Utility Model Act shall be deemed legitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If substantive lack of novelty/inventive step is clear, consultation among applicants is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus vs species identity rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A genus invention of a later-filed application is deemed to be identical with a species invention of a prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses identity when claim scope overlaps across genus/species between filings of different dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when filing dates are identical
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the filing dates of Invention A and Invention B are the same, if they are deemed substantially the same under comparison assuming each as prior or later filed, they may be deemed identical; but if they are not substantially the same under the reverse assumption, they shall not be deemed identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons must consider both assumptions when filing dates coincide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 32 unpatentable inventions (public order, morality, public health)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding Article 29 (1), no invention that violates public order or sound morals or is likely to harm public health is patentable (Article 32).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an invention falls within patentable subject matter, it may still be refused on public-order/morality/public-health grounds; examiner must assess these aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of public order and morality for patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Public order refers to the general interest of society or country and morality means moral sense generally accepted by society or by a particular group of people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of Article 32 should consider objectives of the Patent Act and societal norms; public order and morality are not treated separately in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of sexual aides under Article 32
rubrics_metrics.description: For inventions relating to sexual aides: i) if the product is quite similar to a specific sexual part of the human body, or ii) if practicing the invention is expected to go beyond sexual morals corresponding to leading consequentially immoral act in public, it is deemed to be against public order or morality. If expected to be conducted in a private place, this rule will not be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must consider similarity to human sexual parts and public vs private use; private-use devices are less likely to be refused on morality grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-body-using inventions and dignity/freedom/harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions using human body which hurt the body consequentially when conducted, inventions blocking inhumanely the freedom of the body, and inventions damaging the dignity of a human being are deemed to be against the public order or morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, inventions using natural human wastes (urine, placenta, blood) extracted safely may be acceptable, except when used as food ingredients which is ethically disallowed under MFDS standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper use does not automatically render invention unpatentable
rubrics_metrics.description: It does not extend the case where an invention is likely to go against public order or morality as a result of improper use of the invention against its original purpose. If apparatus is clearly disclosed and aimed at entertainment (not gambling), it would not contravene public order or morality merely because it could be improperly used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider disclosed purpose and likely intended use, not mere potential for misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of public health risk for manufacturing/process inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claimed invention is a manufacturing process invention, an examiner should consider whether the manufacturing process itself and the product made by the manufacturing process would injure public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even academic reports showing harm do not automatically make invention unpatentable if Ministry of Health and Welfare approves manufacture; examiner should consider whether measures exist to eliminate harmful effects and weigh advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to amend before certified copy of decision to grant (Article 47(1) general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent applicant may amend the specification or any drawing accompanying his/her patent application before a certified copy of a decision to grant a patent under Article 66 is served, subject to specified applicable periods if notice of ground for rejection has been received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are freely allowed before examination starts, but become restricted after notice of grounds for rejection to avoid delay and adding new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods when amendment is allowed after receiving grounds for rejection (Article 47(1) subcases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where notice of ground for rejection has been received, amendment may be made only during applicable periods: 1) within period for submitting written arguments for non-final rejection (or certain other notices), 2) within period for submission of written arguments in response to a final rejection necessitated by amendment, or 3) where a request for re-examination is filed, at the time the request is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different amendment permissions depend on which official notice was received; applicants must act within those designated windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment must be within scope of original disclosure (no new matter) (Article 47(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to the specification or drawings shall be made within the scope of the disclosure of the specification or drawings as originally filed. Foreign-language applications must also be within scope of the final Korean translation as originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition on adding new matter; comparisons use the original filed specification/drawings (or divisional/converted application originals as applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible claim amendment cases (Article 47(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be amended only in the following cases: 1) claims are narrowed by restricting or deleting claims, or adding limitations; 2) clerical errors corrected; 3) ambiguous description clarified; 4) amendment to reinstate previously presented claims under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim amendments that broaden scope are generally disallowed except in tightly-defined reinstatement scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary withdrawal of prior amendments upon final amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent application is amended during the period specified in Article 47(1)1 or 2, all amendments made prior to the final amendment shall be deemed voluntarily withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the final amendment is treated as the applicant's operative amendment for that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-language application amendment conditioned on Korean translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding other provisions, the specification or drawings of a foreign language patent application may be amended only when a Korean translation has been submitted under Article 42-3(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Korean translation submission is a prerequisite for amending foreign-language-filed specs/drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and retroactivity of permitted amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment system designed to address incompleteness and protect applicant rights; where specification is amended during designated period or under specified conditions after filing, the amendment shall take effect retroactively to the original filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactivity supports applicants but is balanced by strict limits to prevent unfair addition of new matter and to protect third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural eligibility to amend (who may amend)
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who can amend the specification or drawing(s) shall be the applicant of the patent application at the time of the amendment. Where two or more applicants exist, not all applicants need undertake amendment proceedings; each applicant may amend the description individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only current applicants may perform amendments; divisional/converted application contexts have specific bases for what counts as 'originally filed'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must be pending to permit amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: For the amendment of a specification or drawing(s), the patent application which is the subject of the amendment shall be pending before KIPO. If the application has been invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or a decision to reject has become final and binding, the amendment shall not be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pendency means KIPO can take administrative actions (e.g., register establishment of a patent right); terminated or registered applications are not amendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive restriction: prohibition of addition of new matter depending on amendment period
rubrics_metrics.description: The addition of new matter shall be prohibited when an amendment is made within the voluntary amendment period before the start of examination or within the period designated for submitting arguments on a non-final rejection. During certain later periods only narrowing of claims and similar limited amendments are permitted; addition of new matter remains prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope of permissible amendment differs by period; later periods impose further restrictions (e.g., only narrowing allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of illegitimate (substantively impermissible) amendments by timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The method to handle an amendment which does not satisfy substantive requirements differs based on amendment periods: e.g., during examination the illegitimate amendment may become a ground for rejection; after registration it may become a ground for invalidation; in some periods the decision may be to refuse to enter the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences (refuse, reject, or invalidation) depend on when the illegitimate amendment was made; see table in guidelines for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of voluntary amendment period
rubrics_metrics.description: The voluntary amendment period refers to the time before the Commissioner serves a certified copy of a decision to grant a patent, except for periods under Article 47(1) subparagraphs. The voluntary amendment period includes the time between applicant's reception of a non-final rejection and examiner's issuance of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an applicant submits an amendment after the examiner has sent out a certified copy of a decision to grant a patent, the amendment shall not be admitted even if the applicant had not yet received the copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period for submission of arguments in reply to rejection (usual duration and extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The period designated for the submission of arguments is commonly two months. The period shall be extended on a request for extension by the applicant according to Article 15(2) of the Patent Act. Where the period exceeds four months, extension may or may not be permitted by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must file amendments within the designated argument-submission period when replying to non-final or final rejections (subject to limits and examiner discretion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reexamination timing and amendment on reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant shall be able to request a reexamination within 30 days from the receipt of a certified copy of a decision to reject and amend the specification or drawing(s) attached to the application upon a request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The period for appeal against a decision to reject can be extended under Article 15(1), so amendments upon reexamination may be made within extended appeal periods if requirements are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning and assessment of 'new matter' (prohibition of addition)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'New matter' refers to a matter which goes beyond the scope of the disclosure of the specification or drawing(s) as originally filed. Matters explicitly described or that a person skilled in the art would recognize as disclosed are not new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment compares the amended specification/drawings (subject of assessment) to the original specification/drawings (subject of comparison). 'Included in the scope of the disclosure' does not require literal identity; it includes what skilled person would clearly recognize from original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment rules: sources not usable as basis for original disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A first country application or a prior-filed application forming the basis of a priority claim shall not correspond to the specification or drawing(s) as originally filed and shall not be used as the basis of assessment in addition of new matter. An abstract shall also not be included in the specification/drawings which form the basis of assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons must use the specification/drawings filed on the filing date; abstracts and priority documents are not substitutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing an incomplete invention considered addition of new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of completing an incomplete invention, the amendment shall be deemed to add new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filling gaps that complete previously incomplete inventions is treated as introducing new matter and is impermissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrowing genus to species: when it constitutes new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment is made to narrow a claim as from a genus to a species, unless the species is supported by the original specification and drawings, or unless one skilled in the art would readily recognize the species from the genus in light of ordinary skill at filing time, it shall be viewed as introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: inserting specific material (e.g., 'ABS') is new matter unless originally disclosed or obvious; specifying 'proximity sensor' for 'sensor detecting rotation' is acceptable if skilled person would intuitively associate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening species to genus and deletion of essential limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment broadens a claim as from a species to a genus, if the genus encompasses other species than the species disclosed and the other species may have different function or effects, the amendment shall constitute introduction of new matter. Deleting limitations described as essential for solving a problem is introduction of new matter; deleting arbitrary limitations unrelated to solving the problem may be allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: changing a detailed structural limitation to a broader term may alter expected effects and be new matter; deleting purely arbitrary limitations may be acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete examples illustrating new-matter assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples provided by guideline: (Ex1) 'transparent plastic plate' amended to 'transparent ABS plastic plate' may introduce new matter unless ABS disclosed/obvious; (Ex2) 'sensor detecting rotation of toothed wheel' amended to 'proximity sensor detecting rotation' acceptable if skilled person would associate; connector shape broadening and traffic control method deletion examples illustrate when effects change and new matter arises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these examples to guide practical determinations of support/obviousness and to detect impermissible introduction of new technical content.
